identityReview: Indian industrialist Venu Srinivasan, not his son Sudarshan Venu. Birth date confirmed by an exchange-hosted company filing. Education, inherited family relationship, historical executive roles and current chairman emeritus title are distinguished.
lifeStatusEvidence: The Economic Times reports a November 11, 2026 joint letter signed by Srinivasan and Vijay Singh; relevant article text was read. This is recent attributed activity, not an inference from a missing death field.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Opened primary company and university material, JUSE award list, government gazette and High Court text; read current reporting and governance research. Search snippets were only corroboration where the full annual report exceeded the fetch limit.
corrections: Exchange-hosted 2006–2007 annual report, printed page 5: birth 11 December 1952; engineering degree from Madras; Sundaram-Clayton managing director from May 1979; TVS Motor managing director from 1986 and chairman from July 2002. Historical titles are not treated as all current.
Purdue explicitly identifies him as a 1977 management master’s alumnus. Prefer this to company shorthand MBA; do not turn later honorary doctorates into research degrees.

JUSE announcement dated 1 October 2019 lists the distinct overseas dissemination and promotion service award. This is separate from company Deming awards and from the Deming Prize for Individuals category.

February 2022 reporting establishes the effective date of 1 April 2022, with managing director retained. The earlier January 2023 succession plan was superseded. Official annual report search excerpt corroborated the date; full PDF fetch failed because of size.

Read the High Court judgment, including operative paragraphs 73–74. It quashed the case against the petitioner in C.C.No.1 of 2023; this is not a criminal conviction or a finding that all later challenges ended.

Read October 14, 2026 court reporting. Allegations, denial and challenge to quashing are distinguished. Later listed hearing was not presumed to occur, and no final outcome after this report was established. Case-number details in the report are themselves unverified.
Read November 16 PTI report about Lakshmi’s partition demand. A demand or asserted inheritance entitlement is not a court award, ownership finding or completed partition.

Read InGovern’s report to include Srinivasan’s opposing position that these were personal assets allocated fairly. InGovern explicitly does not adjudicate private family claims; company financial performance does not establish legal ownership.

Read November 14 reporting of the November 11 letter signed by Srinivasan and Vijay Singh. This supports recent activity; interpretations of Tata governance remain attributed positions, not judicial findings.

Official board biography identifies chairman emeritus and quality-management work. Do not repeat its compressed attribution of the same 2002 Deming date to two different companies, or its inconsistent Korean award year/president pairing.

Read the November 8, 2021 government gazette notification 190, naming him under Padma Bhushan for the award year 2020. Do not confuse the award year, notification date and media report date, or call this Padma Vibhushan.
sourceReview.limits: No final court outcome after the October 14 report was established. Family ownership claims remain disputed. No claim that corporate or personal awards establish the truth of contested allegations. No full audio/video or portrait inspection.
